---
title: "Installing current Quarto on Arch Linux"
status: mature
---

There are two reasonable ways to install Quarto on Arch: use an AUR package, or use Quarto's official Linux tarball. The old version of this note assumed the Arch package route was unavailable; that is no longer true.

## option 1: AUR

The AUR currently has `quarto-cli-bin`:

```bash
yay -S quarto-cli-bin
```

This is the simplest Arch-style installation, but the AUR package can lag behind Quarto's current upstream release.

## option 2: official tarball

Quarto documents a user-local tarball installation on Linux. Download the current Linux x86_64 tarball from the [Quarto release page](https://quarto.org/docs/download/release), then extract it under `~/opt` and link the executable into `~/.local/bin`.

For a downloaded file named `quarto-VERSION-linux-amd64.tar.gz`:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/opt ~/.local/bin
tar -C ~/opt -xzf ~/Downloads/quarto-VERSION-linux-amd64.tar.gz
ln -sfn ~/opt/quarto-VERSION/bin/quarto ~/.local/bin/quarto
```

Make sure `~/.local/bin` is on `PATH`, then verify:

```bash
quarto check
```

Using a user-local install avoids the old `sudo mv ... /opt/quarto` setup and does not require maintaining a root-owned updater script.
